敏.meaning: A pickpocket at the market reaches for an old lady's purse, but <part>every</part> time his hand gets close she snaps open her <part>fan</part> and swats his knuckles, without looking up from the melons. He gives up and slinks away. That's quick-witted <kanji>cleverness</kanji>.
敏.on: Still not looking up, she sweeps the melon rind he tripped on into a rubbish <sound>bin</sound>.
敏.kun: She keeps her coins in her <sound>sa</sound>ri, a <sound>to</sound>ffee tin and a jar with an <sound>ee</sound>l in it.

鋭.meaning: An <part>imp</part> with nothing to do sharpens a <part>gold</part> pencil all day: fine enough to pop bubbles across the room, then fine enough to split a raindrop in two. By evening the tip is too <kanji>pointed</kanji> to write with.
鋭.on: So he uses it to carve a tiny smiling face on an <sound>a</sound>corn.
鋭.kun: Then he spears <sound>su</sound>shi off a <sound>roo</sound>k's plate and a sardine off a <sound>do</sound>lphin's.

脂.meaning: A chef opens a diner on the <part>moon</part> and fries everything in bacon drippings. The astronauts all call it <part>delicious</part>, but each one floats home a little rounder, and the plates glisten for weeks. The secret ingredient is <kanji>fat</kanji>.
脂.on: The chef scrubs the greasy pans with an old knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
脂.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs an astronaut, licking grease off a cook<sound>boo</sound>k full of <sound>ra</sound>men recipes.

掲.meaning: A shipwrecked sailor jams his <part>anchor</part> upright in the sand and lashes a striped <part>sunshade</part> to its top, then waves the whole thing until a passing plane spots it. When you're lost, the smart thing is to <kanji>put up</kanji> something bright.
掲.on: The pilot drops him a birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke on a little parachute.
掲.kun: 'Stay <sound>ca</sound>lm,' he tells a <sound>ca</sound>rp in a rock pool, and holds the sunshade higher.

坂.meaning: A grumpy mole is <part>anti</part> anything flat. All night he shovels <part>soil</part> under one end of the bowling green until the whole lawn tilts, and the bowls roll off into the pond. By morning the green is a <kanji>slope</kanji>.
坂.on: The bowlers sit at the bottom eating toast and <sound>hon</sound>ey while the bowls dry.
坂.kun: A lady in a <sound>sa</sound>ri sleds down it on a <sound>ca</sound>rdboard tray.

雇.meaning: A baker hires a <part>sparrow</part> to work the shop <part>door</part>: it pecks the handle to open it, chirps hello to every customer and takes payment in crumbs. Sales double. It's the best bird she ever chose to <kanji>employ</kanji>.
雇.on: On weekends she also takes on a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala to guard the cream buns.
雇.kun: She pays the sparrow in <sound>ya</sound>rn and sticky <sound>to</sound>ffee, which it loves.
